title: Two Sum
oneLinerQuestion: Find indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Two Sum problem asks us to find two indices in an array whose values add up to a specified target. A brute-force nested search compares every possible pair in O(N^2) time. We can optimize this to O(N) by framing the problem around the equation: complement = target - nums[i]. By remembering previously visited numbers in a hash map, we can check for this complement in O(1) average lookup time.

- Step 1: Hash Map Initialization — We initialize an empty hash map (or dictionary) where keys store visited array elements and values store their corresponding indices. This memory structure acts as an instant lookup cache for past values.

- Step 2: Linear Traversal — We iterate through the array using an index 'i' from 0 to N - 1. In a single pass, each element nums[i] is evaluated as a candidate for the final pair.

- Step 3: Complement Calculation — For the current value nums[i], we calculate complement = target - nums[i]. This value represents the exact counterpart required to achieve the target sum.

- Step 4: Constant-Time Complement Lookup — We query the hash map to see if 'complement' already exists. If found, a valid pair has been identified: map.get(complement) gives the earlier index and 'i' gives the current index. We immediately return [map.get(complement), i].

- Step 5: Element Insertion — If the complement is not present in the map, we record the current number by inserting map.set(nums[i], i). This makes nums[i] available as a potential complement for subsequent numbers in the array.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) because the array is traversed only once and hash map lookups take O(1) time on average. Space Complexity: O(N) to store up to N elements and indices in the hash map.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION twoSum(nums, target):
    seen = HASH_MAP()
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        complement = target - nums[i]
        IF complement IN seen THEN RETURN [seen[complement], i]
        seen[nums[i]] = i
    END FOR
    RETURN []
END FUNCTION
